touches.text: A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.
The instance is a number; a singleton is 0. A bare name addresses instance 0 (`cc` means `cc 0`); the number is written only when it isn't 0.

Ownership. The librarian owns every tree and delegates some to the devices that learn. EVERYTHING THAT LEARNS USING OUR GRAPH TREES IS A DELEGATE (CodeMother, chart and any learning block are examples, not a list), and each holds its trees by the librarian's delegation (Law 6: delegation through the owner's gate). WHY: two holders with different weights over the same nodes have different perspectives and can debate points, and the librarian, asked anything, can look at the query from both.
Trees as tables, permanent: each asks one question, with the weights in its leaves. A tree past 5K leaves is calved at its dominant attractors, a deterministic code shear.

Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged. [Q#90: A proof's seal is one record, so the newest OS to seal replaces the other's, and a proof with teeth for both OSes reds on every single OS. Measured 2026-11-12: a Windows reseal of a mixed proof overwrote the Linux seal. Do seals go per OS (validations/<os>/, or an OS key in the record), or is one OS the sealing box?]
PURPOSE: Wrap a service so there is exactly one way to it.
WHY: One way means one place to authenticate, meter, route and gate, and one place RULE 1 can be enforced by physics (import_sieve, 17.13).

The only way to the inference host; anything that goes around it is an error. WHY: its two points are to find the cheapest model powerful enough for each request, and to train the graph trees on the results.
Device name on the command line and bus: inference.
Every call makes an inference ticket (3.4.2): trees first, then the cheapest route the nest finds.
A request seen before is answered from the stored answer, if it still holds, and the host is not touched. That untouched call is compilation.

The stored answers are learning, so they live in the memory model: a tree the proxy holds by the librarian's delegation, asking "what did this request answer?". An answer is found by its exact request and carries no embedding (4.3.1.6). The meter (every call, its verdict and cost) is not learning: it is metrics (17.27). The inference ticket, a file in the logs tree on the 30 day clock, is only for debugging.
TOOLS: base, import_sieve; database client. MACHINES: route, nest.
VERBS: infer, embed, resolve, calls. COMMANDS: cairn inference show.
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. WHY: enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1 by physics. USERS: CodeMother, the inference proxy.
